findings.claim: DISPATCH-NOTE.md acceptance checklist item (i) still contains the phrase 'rulesets API + admin flags' as the stated justification for the gh 2.40 floor. COMP-003 corrected this in the script (inline comment now reads 'unified branch-protection PUT shape… has been stable since gh 2.x; anything older risks API drift') but the corresponding dispatch-note line was not updated, creating a divergence between the source of truth and the acceptance checklist.
findings.evidence: DISPATCH-NOTE.md line 33: 'Header asserts `gh --version >= 2.40` (rulesets API + admin flags)'. Script lines 83-85: '# 2.40 floor — the unified branch-protection PUT shape used here / # has been stable since gh 2.x; anything older risks API drift.' The two descriptions conflict.
findings.impact: Future operators or reviewers reading the dispatch note will encounter inaccurate justification for the version floor. If a reviewer asks 'does 020G use the rulesets API?' the dispatch note says yes; the script says no. Documentation debt that compounds across future 020G-derived slices.
findings.mitigation: Update DISPATCH-NOTE.md item (i): replace 'rulesets API + admin flags' with 'unified branch-protection PUT shape (stable since gh 2.x; older versions risk API drift)' to match the script comment.

findings.claim: DISPATCH-NOTE.md acceptance checklist item (ii) describes --no-enforce-admins as 'opts out with stderr warning.' Post fix-round-1 (SAF-003 closure), --no-enforce-admins is silently ignored — exits with error code 2 — unless --i-understand-this-bypasses-the-gate is also set. The 5-second pause and visible warning only fire when both flags are present. The dispatch note's wording understates the enforcement and omits the confirmation-flag requirement entirely.
findings.evidence: DISPATCH-NOTE.md line 37: '--no-enforce-admins opts out with stderr warning.' Script lines 174-188: if ENFORCE_ADMINS != true AND ACK_ADMIN_BYPASS != 1, exits 2 with 'error: --no-enforce-admins ignored without --i-understand-this-bypasses-the-gate'. The 5-second pause + warning block only executes when ACK_ADMIN_BYPASS=1.
findings.impact: An operator consulting the dispatch-note checklist before running 020G will believe --no-enforce-admins produces a warning and proceeds. In reality it exits non-zero unless the explicit acknowledgement flag is also set. The discrepancy could cause adoption confusion and is the most operationally significant of the dispatch-note staleness items.
findings.mitigation: Update DISPATCH-NOTE.md item (ii): '--no-enforce-admins silently exits non-zero (error) unless --i-understand-this-bypasses-the-gate is also supplied; with both flags set, a 5-second pause + visible warning precedes the apply (per SAF-003 closure).'

findings.claim: D-035 rationale and the script header (lines 44-48) cite D-022 as the upstream decision-chain anchor for the required-context default 'policy-check / scp/policy-check'. However, D-033 ('WP-SCP-022 020D2.1 reconciliation') is the decision that corrected the context-name format from the bare 'scp/policy-check' (WP-SCP-020 020B(xi) original spec) to the rendered 'policy-check / scp/policy-check'. Since 020G inherits this exact string as its REQUIRED_CONTEXT default, D-033 belongs in the reference chain for both D-035 and the script header.
findings.evidence: Script line 105: REQUIRED_CONTEXT="${SCP_REQUIRED_CONTEXT:-policy-check / scp/policy-check}". Script header lines 44-45: 'Reference: docs/DECISIONS.md D-022 (federation-primitive adoption); D-035 (this slice's invocation procedure)' — D-033 absent. D-033 content: 'Required-check context name correction: WP-SCP-020 020B(xi) specified `scp/policy-check`... updated to `policy-check / scp/policy-check`.' D-035 rationale symmetry list: D-030/D-031/D-032/D-034 — D-033 absent.
findings.impact: Decision-chain gap: the provenance of the context-name default is not traceable from the script or from D-035. A future slice or autonomous agent modifying the context-name default cannot determine why it differs from the WP-SCP-020 020B(xi) spec without independently discovering D-033.
findings.mitigation: Add D-033 to the script header reference block: 'D-033 (020D2.1 context-name correction: rendered check-run name, not bare scp/policy-check context).' Add D-033 to D-035 rationale cross-references alongside D-032.

findings.claim: The CI guard error message at line 55 says 'Set --plan if you need a dry-run from CI.' However, the CI guard executes unconditionally at lines 54-57 before argument parsing. --plan is not evaluated until line 154. The script always exits 1 in CI regardless of whether --plan was supplied. The message actively misleads an operator about a non-functional remediation path.
findings.evidence: Script lines 54-57: unconditional exit 1 when CI=true or GITHUB_ACTIONS=true, with message 'Set --plan if you need a dry-run from CI.' Argument parsing loop begins at line 143. No pre-guard --plan check exists.
findings.impact: An operator with CI=true in their local shell (a common developer convention for testing CI-shaped behaviour) who supplies --plan will receive exit 1 with a suggestion that --plan helps, but it does not. The operator faces a confusing loop: the message prescribes --plan; --plan does not change the outcome. Minor blast radius since the primary use case (local terminal, no CI vars set) is unaffected.
findings.mitigation: Either (a) remove the --plan suggestion from the CI guard message: '020G refuses to run in CI: this is an attended bootstrap script. Unset CI/GITHUB_ACTIONS and run from your local terminal.' Or (b) parse --plan before the CI guard and allow CI+--plan as a legitimate non-mutating dry-run path by skipping the CI exit when PLAN_ONLY is set from a pre-guard argument scan.

findings.claim: The Bootstrap-only header (lines 22-48) lists three operator responsibilities: '--plan first', 'review the diff between before-state and after-state', and 'paste the emitted markdown log entry… and merge.' It does not state that the log block is ALSO emitted on verification failure. The script explicitly emits the log on failure ('Even on failure, capture an invocation log entry so the audit trail records the failure') and then exits non-zero. An operator seeing verification FAIL output might assume the script produced no useful output and skip the log commit.
findings.evidence: Script lines 306-313: '# fall through to log emission so an audit entry exists' with explanatory echo block. Script header lines 28-34: log-commit bullet reads 'paste the emitted markdown log entry into… and merge' — no mention of failure case.
findings.impact: If an operator skips the log commit after a verification failure, the audit trail has no record of the partial apply, defeating the SAF-010 closure intent. The risk is concrete: partial applies (e.g., unified PUT succeeded but required_signatures POST failed) are precisely the cases where an audit entry is most valuable.
findings.mitigation: Add a sentence to the Bootstrap-only header's log-commit bullet: 'This applies on both success and failure — the script emits the log block even when verification fails so the audit trail records partial applies and post-mortem state.'

Estate pattern (project_020c1_tracked_forward.md, TF-005..TF-008) requires deferred items to carry explicit TF entries so they are not silently lost across session-bounded amnesia.
